sentences.text:
The petitioners are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 143, 147,
323, 504, 506, 498(A) R/w Section 149 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. The summary of the charge sheet is that, the De-facto complainant is the legally wedded wife of accused No.1, accused No.2 is the brother-in-law, accused No.3 is the mother-in-law and accused Nos.4 and 5 are the sister-in-laws of the De-facto complainant and they subjected her to cruelty both physically and mentally and also a demand was made to bring money from her parental home.
3. The cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate of the aforesaid offences is impugned in this petition.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1- State and the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
5.

Perusal of the charge sheet material indicates that, petitioner Nos.2 to 5/accused Nos.2 to 5 are residing separately and except omnibus and general allegations, there are no specific allegations as against accused Nos.2 to 5 as to how and in what manner they subjected the De-facto complainant to cruelty and also a demand was made to bring the money from the parental home.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1417 6.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar reported in (2022)
6 SCC 599, at para 18 has held as follows:
"18.

entities.text:
Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar reported in (2022)
6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."

However, in respect of petitioner No.1/accused No.1, there are certain specific allegations and the veracity of the allegations can be considered at the time of trial and at this stage, the same cannot be gone into.

sentences.text: In view of the preceding analysis, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate of the aforesaid offences as against petitioner Nos.2 to 5/accused Nos.2 to 5 only on the basis of omnibus and general allegations is impermissible, and the continuation of the criminal proceedings against them will be an abuse of process of law, since the probability of their NC: 2023:KHC-K:1417 conviction is remote and bleak.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Criminal petition insofar as it relates to petitioner No.1/accused No.1 is dismissed.
ii. Criminal petition insofar as it relates to petitioner Nos.2 to 5/accused Nos.2 to 5 is allowed.
iii. The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.1517/2020, pending on the file of Civil Judge and JMFC, Shorapur (arising out of Crime No.46/2022, registered by Shorapur Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 143, 147, 323,
504, 506, 498(A) R/w Section 149 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act), insofar as it relates to petitioner Nos.2 to 5/accused Nos.2 to 5 is hereby quashed.
iv. Learned Magistrate to proceed against petitioner No.1/accused No.1 on the available material on record without being influenced by any observation made in this order.
Sd/-
